diagnostic_evidence.quote: It should be noticed that the strong analysis of the data space spanned by the solution trajectory depends on the initial regularity, which is similar as in the hyperbolic case.
By the chain rule, one can see that its mass is preserved over time

issues.failure_explanation: The introduction announces as a finding that the (strong) data space of the stochastic Schrödinger solution admits only polynomial-dimensional approximation, in contrast with the logarithmic dimension for the mean. Section 3.2.3 contains no result, proof or lower bound for the strong data space; the only supporting sentence is a heuristic remark that the analysis 'depends on the initial regularity'. A lower bound on approximation dimension is a nontrivial statement that is nowhere established.

failure_location.quote: whereas the data space spanned by the solution itself only admits polynomial-dimensional approximation.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Either prove a lower bound on the dimension needed to approximate the solution trajectory (e.g., using mass conservation and unitarity of e^{i L t}) or withdraw the claim and state it as a conjecture/heuristic.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised 'most intriguing' dichotomy between mean and pathwise data spaces of the Schrödinger equation is not established; the claim in the introduction and the corresponding statement in the contributions list are unsupported.
issues.title: Unsupported claim that the Schrödinger solution data space admits only polynomial-dimensional approximation
issues.why_classification: A contained new argument (a dimension lower bound) or a retraction of a headline claim is needed; the rest of the paper does not depend on it.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: \frac {(2\pi)^{\frac d2}}{t_2-t_1}  \mathbb E \Big[\operatorname{Arg} \Big(\Big|\frac {\widehat u(t_2, \xi)}{\widehat u(t_1, \xi)}\Big|\Big)\Big]& =\sum_{|\alpha|\le p_1, \alpha \; \text{odd}} a_{\alpha}(\bi \xi)^{\alpha}\bi^{-1}.

issues.failure_explanation: In the multiplicative case the argument of \widehat u(t_2,\xi)/\widehat u(t_1,\xi) contains the random term \sum_{odd} b_\beta(i\xi)^\beta i^{-1}(W(t_2)-W(t_1)). The Brownian increment is Gaussian with unbounded support, so for every fixed t_2-t_1>0 and every \xi with a nonzero odd-order diffusion coefficient, this term exceeds \pi in absolute value with positive probability. On that event the principal-value Arg differs from the right-hand side of \eqref{mul-ide-2} by a nonzero multiple of 2\pi, so \eqref{mul-ide-2} fails pathwise and the expectation identity \eqref{dri-mul-ide2} is false (the wrapped Gaussian has expectation different from the drift part). Smallness of t_2-t_1 shrinks but never removes the ambiguity, since the drift signal also scales with t_2-t_1. Hence the odd-order a_\alpha are not exactly determined from two snapshots by the stated argument.

failure_location.quote: Notice that for $|t_2-t_1|>0$ sufficiently small, the phase ambiguity in \eqref{mul-ide-2} can be removed.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Either restrict the multiplicative statement to diffusion operators with only even-order terms (so the phase is deterministic), or replace the principal Arg by the expectation of a continuous branch of log along the path on [t_1,t_2] (which needs path data rather than two snapshots), or state identification of the odd coefficients only up to an exponentially small error in (t_2-t_1)^{-1}.
issues.overall_effect: The multiplicative-noise part of Proposition prop-drift-identification (exact identification of odd-order drift coefficients from two time points) is unproved and, as an exact identity, false whenever \mathcal G has odd-order terms; the additive case and the even-order coefficients are unaffected.
issues.title: Phase ambiguity cannot be removed in the multiplicative-noise drift identification
issues.why_classification: A comparable result survives under an added structural hypothesis or with modified data requirements, but the stated two-snapshot exact-identification claim in the general multiplicative case must be weakened.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: By taking $V$ as the linear space containing $V_1\cup V_2$, we complete the proof for any $t\in [0,T]$.

issues.failure_explanation: The statement quantifies 'for any t there exists V' and measures the error in L^2(\Omega;H). The proof constructs V_1 from vectors containing the random factors c_k and e^{q_k W(t)}, and V_2 from (z_k+\mathcal L/2)^{-1}e^{\mathcal L t/2+\mathcal G W(t)}u_0; both spaces depend on \omega and on t. If V is allowed to be random and t-dependent, the statement is trivial (V=span{u(t,\omega)} has dimension 1 and zero error), so the logarithmic dimension carries no content. If V is required to be deterministic (as the L^2(\Omega;H) norm suggests) or uniform in t (as the comparison with the hyperbolic Lemma lem:added-1, which uses one space for the whole trajectory, requires), the proof does not deliver it: a deterministic V for fixed small t would need polynomially many modes, and no uniform-in-t space is constructed. The same defect occurs in the additive-case proof in Appendix sec-appendix-add-data (V_4,V_5,V_6 are stochastic-integral-dependent and t-dependent).

failure_location.quote: For any $t\in [0,T],$ there exists a linear space $V\subset H$ of dimension $C_{\mathcal L}|\log(\epsilon)|^2$ such that

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must formulate the theorem with a space V that is either deterministic or a single (possibly random) space valid for all t in [0,T], and prove the logarithmic dimension bound for that space, which the present construction (pointwise in t, driven by e^{\mathcal G W(t)}) does not do.
issues.overall_effect: The parabolic data-space result (both noise cases) and the paper's stated dichotomy 'parabolic: O(|log ε|^2) versus hyperbolic: polynomial' are not established; the corresponding claims in the abstract, introduction and conclusion are unsupported.
issues.title: Parabolic data-space theorem: approximating space is random and time-dependent, making the statement vacuous or unproved
issues.why_classification: As stated the result is vacuous, and the only meaningful reformulations require a new argument that the source does not provide and that may fail for unbounded \mathcal G; the central theoretical comparison rests on it.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Since $X_{s,t}(\cdot)$ is $\mathcal C^{p}$-differentiable, one can also show that $G(s,t)$ is $\mathcal C^{p}$-differentiable since $c(\cdot)$ and its derivatives up to order $p$ are bounded thanks to the compactness of $\mathcal D$.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof derives eigenvalue decay for the time kernel G from its smoothness and then uses a common sequence \lambda_j for both K and G. For a deterministic u, K=UU^* and G=U^*U share nonzero spectra, but for random u one has K=\mathbb E[UU^*] and G=\mathbb E[U^*U], which in general have different spectra (e.g. u=\eta_1 f_1 g+\eta_2 f_2 g with f_1\perp f_2, independent standardized \eta_i gives spec(K)={2}, spec(G)={1,1}). Thus the equality above and the transfer of the decay o(j^{-(p+1)}) from G to K is invalid. Moreover, the claimed C^p regularity of G in (s,t) is asserted from spatial C^p regularity of the flow; time regularity of \mathbb E[u_0(X_{t,0}(x))u_0(X_{s,0}(x))] comes from the Kolmogorov equation and costs two spatial derivatives per time derivative, so C^p in time does not follow from u_0\in C^p.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Work directly with the spatial kernel K: prove K\in C^p(\mathcal D^2) from the C^p regularity of the flow and moment bounds, apply the eigenvalue decay for positive C^p kernels on a d-dimensional domain, and restate the dimension as o(\epsilon^{-2d/p}) (which coincides with the claim for d=1).
issues.overall_effect: The dimension bound o(\epsilon^{-2/p}) for the hyperbolic data space is not proved as stated; the rate may change (with d and with the true time regularity), affecting the parabolic-versus-hyperbolic comparison.
issues.title: Hyperbolic lemma: spectra of K and G do not coincide for random u, and temporal regularity of G is unjustified
issues.why_classification: A contained replacement argument yields a recognizably comparable result, possibly with a dimension-dependent rate; no global restructuring is needed.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: For any $t\in [0,T],$ there exists a linear space $V\subset H

issues.failure_explanation: The object approximated, \mathbb E u(t), is a single deterministic element of H_{\mathbb C} for each fixed t. Since the proposition quantifies 'for any t there exists V', it is trivially true with V=span{\mathbb E u(t)} of dimension 1; the logarithmic dimension bound carries no information. The proof indeed builds t-dependent spaces (V_t, and in the large-time regime spaces spanned by e^{i\mathcal L t}(z_k+\mathcal G^*\mathcal G/2)^{-1}\mathbb E u_0), and the small-time space V_t even contains the random coefficients c_k although the target is deterministic. A meaningful version (one space of dimension O(|log ε|^2) approximating \mathbb E u(t) for all t in [0,T]) is not proved and is doubtful under the stated hypothesis \lim(\Re\lambda_k-2\Re(q_k)^2)>0, since then the generator i\mathcal L-\mathcal G^2/2 is not sectorial and the unitary factor e^{i\mathcal L t} prevents the resolvent-based space from being t-independent.

failure_location.quote: \|\mathbb E u(t)-\mathbb E P_{V}u(t)\|_{L^2(\Omega;H_{\mathbb C})}\lesssim  \epsilon (1+\|u_0\|_{L^2(\Omega;H_{\mathbb C})})

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must restate the proposition with a single space V valid uniformly in t (or another nontrivial quantifier structure) and provide a proof handling the unitary factor e^{i\mathcal L t}.
issues.overall_effect: The 'logarithmic dimension of the mean data space' finding for the stochastic Schrödinger equation is not established; the corresponding prose in the introduction and Section 3.2.3 is unsupported.
issues.title: Schrödinger mean data-space proposition is vacuous as stated (pointwise-in-t space for a deterministic vector)
issues.why_classification: The stated result has no content and the intended nontrivial version lacks any supporting argument in the source; no comparable version of the claim survives without new architecture.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The algorithm terminates when the  regression error does not improve.

issues.failure_explanation: The loop breaks only on a strict increase of the residual. When the selected index set \mathcal I^{\ell+1} equals \mathcal I^{\ell} (the fixed point the algorithm aims for), Steps 2–3 return the same coefficients and the residual is exactly equal, so the break condition is false and the loop repeats identically forever. The prose contract 'terminates when the regression error does not improve' is not implemented by the pseudo-code; the numerical section relies on an external iteration cap of 100 not present in the algorithm.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Change the stopping test to '\geq' (or add an explicit maximum iteration count / support-stabilization check) so the loop exits when the residual fails to strictly decrease.
issues.overall_effect: As written, Algorithm QSPalgo does not terminate on convergence; the same flaw is present in the reproduced SP pseudo-code (SPalgo). The output contract is only met with an unstated iteration cap.
issues.title: QSP stopping rule never triggers once the support stabilizes (non-termination)
issues.why_classification: A one-line local fix restores the intended behavior with no loss of any claimed guarantee.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: which is a standard normal variable with  cumulative distribution function (CDF) $\Phi$ under the null hypothesis. Then for some significance level $p^* \in (0,1)$

issues.failure_explanation: For a standard normal Z_N and a significance level p^*<1/2 (the usual case), \Phi^{-1}(p^*)<0, so the condition 2|Z_N|\geq\Phi^{-1}(p^*) holds always and the test always declares multiplicative noise, while 2|Z_N|<\Phi^{-1}(p^*)/2 never holds. Even for p^*>1/2 the two conditions are not complementary (there is a gap between \Phi^{-1}(p^*)/2 and \Phi^{-1}(p^*)) and the factor 2 on |Z_N| has no justification for a two-sided test on a standard normal statistic. The procedure as stated does not implement the described level-p^* test.

failure_location.quote: we decide that the diffusion part contains multiplicative noise if $2|Z_N|\geq \Phi^{-1}(p^*)$, and it is only additive if $2|Z_N|<\Phi^{-1}(p^*)/2$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the rule by the standard two-sided test: declare multiplicative noise if |Z_N|\geq\Phi^{-1}(1-p^*/2) and additive otherwise.
issues.overall_effect: The additive-noise detection procedure of Section sec_stat_detect is not a valid hypothesis test as written; its stated false-positive control is not delivered.
issues.title: Ill-formed decision thresholds in the additive-noise detection test
issues.why_classification: The fix is a routine, local correction of the threshold formula that preserves the intended procedure and its guarantee.
